biggest_catch: This is not a lump-sum bonus: it is a limited-time 3% dining welcome offer on up to $6,000 of dining spend in the first 6 months, plus a separate $25 statement credit for enrolling in autopay. Year-one math: the card normally earns 1.5% on dining, so the incremental bonus is the extra 1.5% on up to $6,000, which is up to $90, plus the $25 autopay credit, for up to about $115 total in welcome value with no annual fee. Only claim this if you were already going to spend on dining; never spend extra on restaurants to chase the 3%. It is positioned for limited or new credit history, but the hard inquiry, the 5/24 pattern, and the ~20%+ APR warning all still apply.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra on dining just to chase the 3% rate, because eating out you would not have paid for turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: the incremental welcome value is the extra 1.5% over the card's normal 1.5% dining rate on up to $6,000 in the first 6 months, which is up to $90, plus a $25 autopay statement credit, for up to about $115 total. The cap matters: dining spend above $6,000 in the first 6 months earns the normal rate.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.

The 3% rate applies only to dining at restaurants, including takeout and eligible delivery services, and only on up to $6,000 spent in the first 6 months from account opening. Other purchases earn the normal 1.5%.
The $25 statement credit is separate and requires enrolling in autopay; do not confuse it with the 3% dining offer.

Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit. The account must be open and not in default when rewards post.
